title: While Thee I Seek, Protecting Power
description: While Thee I Seek, Protecting Power in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Helen Maria Williams wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 95, “Habitual Devotion”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: While Thee I seek, pro-tect-ing Power! Be my vain wish-es stilled; And may this con-se-cra-ted hour With bet-ter hopes be filled.

lines: While Thee I seek, protecting Power!
Be my vain wishes stilled;
And may this consecrated hour
With better hopes be filled.
Thy love the powers of thought bestowed;
To Thee my thoughts would soar;
Thy mercy o'er my life has flowed;
That mercy I adore!
In each event of life, how clear
Thy ruling hand I see!
Each blessing to my soul more dear,
Because conferred by Thee.
In every joy that crowns my days,
In every pain I bear,
My heart shall find delight in praise,
Or seek relief in prayer.
When gladness wings my favored hour,
Thy love my thoughts shall fill;
Resigned, when storms of sorrow lower,
My soul shall meet Thy will.
My lifted eye, without a tear,
The gathering storm shall see;
My steadfast heart shall know no fear;
That heart shall rest on Thee!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Helen Maria Williams died in 1827.
credits: Words by Helen Maria Williams (1759–1827), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
